why: After each chunk the received bytes are a merge-intervals result, with the extra rule that adjacent ranges (end + 1 == next start) also merge. Keep the current disjoint sorted list and insert each new chunk into it.
hints: After every arrival you need a Merge Intervals answer. Do you have to merge everything from scratch, or is the previous snapshot already sorted and disjoint?

Insert the new chunk into the existing sorted disjoint list: everything ending before start - 1 stays left, everything starting after end + 1 stays right, and everything in between is swallowed into one range.
Per arrival: one linear pass (or bisect) over the current ranges, O(k) each, O(n^2) total for n <= 2000. Serialize each range as f"{s}:{e}".
pitfalls: Adjacent ranges merge: [1,3] then [4,6] becomes 1:6. The test is next.start <= cur.end + 1.
Values go up to 10^18; fine in Python but beware an array-of-bytes approach.
A chunk can bridge two existing ranges at once (example 2's [2,8]).
